extra.message: CsvService.impMgrMap() builds native SQL by concatenating the CSV-supplied employeeEmail/managerEmail values directly into the query string ("SELECT id FROM employees WHERE email = '" + empEmail + "'"), then executes it via em.createNativeQuery(...).getResultList(). User-controlled CSV content reaches the SQL parser unescaped, allowing SQL injection (e.g. ' OR '1'='1).

cwe: CWE-89: SQL Injection

extra.message: importFeedLegacy() deserializes the attacker-supplied 'definition' request parameter with XStream after calling xstream.addPermission(AnyTypePermission.ANY). Allowing any type to be deserialized from untrusted XML enables gadget-chain remote code execution (CWE-502). The XML is taken straight from a request parameter.

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: printDocument() passes the user-controlled X-Print-Queue header value ('queue') into Runtime.getRuntime().exec(new String[]{"sh","-c","lp -d " + queue + " " + ...}). Because it is invoked through 'sh -c', shell metacharacters in the queue name allow arbitrary OS command execution.

cwe: CWE-78: OS Command Injection

extra.message: extractText() concatenates the user-supplied 'lang' request parameter into a shell command executed via ProcessBuilder("sh","-c", "tesseract ... -l " + lang). Shell metacharacters in 'lang' permit arbitrary command execution.

cwe: CWE-78: OS Command Injection

extra.message: evaluateDeduction() obtains the BeanShell ('bsh') scripting engine and evaluates the attacker-supplied 'formula' request body directly (engine.eval(formula)). BeanShell evaluates arbitrary Java code, so this is remote code execution. Reached via POST /admin/compensation/deductions/preview.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: hrisCard() parses the caller-supplied 'assertion' with Jwts.parserBuilder().setSigningKey(...).parseClaimsJwt(...). parseClaimsJwt parses an UNSIGNED (alg=none) JWT and never verifies the signature, and the code ignores the configured signing key for verification. Any authenticated employee can forge an assertion whose 'sub' is another employee's email, and the endpoint then returns that employee's full name, email and salary history (compensationService.history). This is a signature-verification/authentication bypass (CWE-347) leading to broken access control.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: payslipCard() derives the target employee id from the client-controlled 'hrp_operator' cookie (empId = Long.valueOf(operator.substring(0, operator.indexOf(':')))) and then loads and displays that employee's record and compensation history without any ownership check. A user can set the cookie to any employee id (e.g. '2:x') and view another employee's salary data. The cookie itself is set from an unauthenticated X-Portal-Operator header in DashboardController.portalEntry.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: syncAttributes() binds every submitted request parameter directly onto the authenticated Employee entity with org.apache.commons.beanutils.BeanUtils.populate(me, attributes). Employee exposes setters for role, enabled, email, passwordHash, department, manager, etc. Any authenticated user can POST /profile/attributes?role=HR_ADMIN to set their own role on the session-cached principal and escalate privileges (the principal's Employee object is shared across the session, so role checks then pass).

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: exportPayrollRun() builds the output path with dir.resolve(runRef + ".csv") from the unvalidated 'runRef' request parameter and then Files.write()s to it. No normalization/startsWith check is done (unlike FileStorageService), so runRef values such as '../../etc/foo' escape the intended export directory and write arbitrary files.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: saveSummary() writes a file to dir.resolve(fileName) where 'fileName' is a user-supplied @RequestParam with no path validation or normalization. A manager can supply '../../...' to write files outside the review directory (arbitrary file write).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: listBatchDir() calls Files.list(baseDir.resolve(batchPath)) with the batchPath read from the user-supplied manifest, without normalizing or verifying the result stays under baseDir. A manifest containing '../..' lets a payroll user enumerate arbitrary directories on the server.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: bandFor() parses the attacker-supplied XML 'message' with a default DocumentBuilderFactory (dbf.newDocumentBuilder().parse(new InputSource(new StringReader(message)))). External entity processing, DTDs and external parameter entities are not disabled, so an XML External Entity payload can read local files or trigger SSRF. Reached via POST /admin/compensation/bands/resolve.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: readDocTotals() parses an uploaded payslip as XML using a default DocumentBuilderFactory without disabling DTDs/external entities (dbf.newDocumentBuilder().parse(in)). A crafted payslip XML causes XXE file disclosure or SSRF when the payroll desk views a document's totals. findTotal() uses the same pattern.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: findTotal() builds an XPath expression by concatenating the user-supplied totalName: "//total[@name='" + totalName + "']". An attacker who controls the query file (totalName) can inject XPath to alter the selection and extract/abuse arbitrary nodes from the parsed XML.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')

extra.message: bandFor() concatenates the department value extracted from untrusted XML into an XPath expression: "//band[department='" + dept + "']". Attacker-controlled dept values allow XPath injection against the salary-band catalogue.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')

extra.message: staffEntry() builds the LDAP search filter by concatenating the user-supplied uid: "(&(objectClass=person)(uid=" + uid + "))". Unescaped LDAP filter metacharacters allow LDAP injection, letting the caller broaden/alter the search filter used against the corporate directory (CWE-90).

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')

extra.message: checkCallbackRoute() issues restTemplate.getForObject("https://" + forwardedHost + "/hris/feed-callback") where forwardedHost comes from the client-supplied X-Forwarded-Host header (AdminController.checkFeedRoute). The host is not validated against an allowlist, so an attacker can direct the server to make arbitrary outbound HTTPS requests (SSRF / internal port probing).

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message:
The HR request comment body is rendered with raw EL
${c.body}
instead of , so HTML/JavaScript in the user-supplied comment body is emitted unescaped. An employee can post an HR request comment containing a script payload, which then executes in the HR admin's browser when the request detail page is viewed (stored XSS).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: portalEntry() passes the wildcard path variable 'dest' straight into response.sendRedirect(target) with no validation. A request such as /portal-entry//evil.example.com results in a redirect to an attacker-controlled site (protocol-relative URL), enabling open-redirect phishing.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The filter reflects any request Origin back in Access-Control-Allow-Origin while also setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This allows any website to make credentialed cross-origin requests to the portal and read the responses, defeating the same-origin policy.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: handleUnexpected() puts the exception toString() and full stack trace (Arrays.toString(ex.getStackTrace())) into the model rendered by error/500.jsp, exposing internal class names, file paths and framework details to any user who triggers an unhandled exception. application.yml also sets include-stacktrace/include-message to 'always'.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: All actuator endpoints are exposed (management.endpoints.web.exposure.include: "*") and heapdump, env, beans and configprops are explicitly enabled. SecurityConfig permits /actuator/** without authentication, so unauthenticated users can download the heap (heapdump) and read environment properties including datasource credentials and secrets, and configuration properties.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: GET /api/reference/feed-profile returns the HRIS feed 'signingKey' (payrollFeedService.getSigningKey()) and partner account in a JSON response available to any authenticated user. The interchange/signing key should not be exposed to general staff; it is used to sign outbound payroll feed messages.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: BureauAccessBootstrap creates a production payroll account (bureau.exchange@hrpayroll.example, role PAYROLL_SPECIALIST) whose password is a hardcoded literal "bureau-exchange-2026". Anyone knowing the source can authenticate as this privileged automation account.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The JWT signing/interchange key is a hardcoded byte literal ("hrpayroll-hris-bridge-2026") embedded in source. Combined with the parseClaimsJwt flaw, the key is exposed and reusable; secrets should be externalized to configuration rather than compiled into the artifact.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: SeedDataRunner creates multiple privileged accounts (HR admin, payroll specialist, managers) all using the hardcoded demo password "Password123!" which is also displayed on the login page. If seeding is not disabled in a real deployment these credentials are a full compromise.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The security filter chain disables the X-Frame-Options header (.frameOptions(HeadersConfigurer.FrameOptionsConfig::disable)), so the portal can be embedded in an iframe on any attacker-controlled site and used for clickjacking of authenticated HR actions.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

extra.message: The session cookie is configured with http-only: false and secure: false, and session tracking-modes: url. The JSESSIONID/HRPSESSION cookie is therefore readable from JavaScript (no HttpOnly) and can be sent over plaintext HTTP; URL-based tracking can also leak the session id in URLs, logs and Referer headers.

cwe: CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag

extra.message: The authentication failure handler concatenates the user-supplied 'username' parameter directly into a log message (SIGNIN_LOG.warn("Rejected sign-in attempt for account " + request.getParameter("username") + ...)). Newline/control characters in the username allow log injection/forging of audit lines.

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: applyAssistantReview() feeds employee-controlled evidence text (the attachment contents) into an external LLM prompt and then applies the model's returned action to approve/reject the onboarding task without human confirmation. An employee can embed instructions in the evidence to cause an auto-approval they are not entitled to. The same pattern exists in HrRequestService.applyAssistantTriage().
